newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila bourse gains but still looks for direction.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila bourse gains but still looks for direction.

text.p: Philippine stocks searching for direction inched up on Tuesday on the Dow's overnight rebound as analysts had mixed reaction to news of a 15 percent rise in the first quarter earnings of index heavyweight Ayala Land Inc.

"The bottom line continues to be that the market is really being held hostage by Wall Street," said Louie Bate, managing director for Equities Brokerage Trading at ING Baring Securities Philippines Inc.
In a day of cheerless trading, the main index edged up 16.62 points, or 0.57 percent, to 2,949.46 points, with all sub-sectors waddling up except mining, which dipped 0.62 percent.

Ayala Land announced after trading ended it had posted a first quarter net income of 1.42 billion pesos, up from 1.24 billion in the same period last year but analysts disagreed on what its impact would be on the market.
One analyst said it should improve sentiment in a market recently battered by fears of a price crash in a market reported to be suffering from too much supplies.
But another said Ayala Land's earnings fell below expectation and that, offhand, he doubted it would ease investor anxieties about the sector.
Property stocks Empire East Land Holdings Inc and Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc suffered selldown in late trade. Empire lost 40 centavos for the day and Megaworld 30 centavos.

Among commercial-industrial issues, Benpres Holdings Corp held its gains at close which traders attributed to news it had divested stakes in its media subsidiaries allowing direct foreign investment in Benpres.
After Ayala Land, other blue-chip companies were expected to release their first quarter earnings results later in the week.

"The bottom line is the market will remain very selective," Bate said when asked what impact announcements of first quarter corporate earnings would have on a market still largely driven by sentiment from Wall street.
"The bottom line is the market will remain very selective," he said.
"For some issues, like Ayala, the positive earnings should aid the stock but for others it will take more than just current earnings to convince investors."
